primary_secondary.note: Both: vendor guide presenting DX's own AI Measurement Framework, backed by DX's own benchmark data.

dora_applied.note: DORA metrics only named as complementary to AI metrics, together with DX Core 4.

ai_discussed.note: Framework for measuring utilization, impact and cost of AI coding assistants and agents.

remote_covid.note: Neither mentions remote work or COVID-19.

data_window.claude: no basis (figures from DX Q1 2026 report; longitudinal study over more than a year)
data_window.nlm: no basis (figures from DX Q1 2026 report)
data_window.note: Not stated by either as a data period; both only cite the Q1 2026 report edition.

cat_productivity.note: AI-driven time savings (hours/week), PR throughput, human-equivalent hours; Booking.com 16% throughput gain.

cat_quality.note: Change fail percentage, code maintainability, change confidence; CFR swings up to 2 points.

cat_collaboration.note: Meeting-heavy days and interruption frequency appear in one sentence only (listed by Claude, in an insight by NotebookLM).

cat_satisfaction.note: Developer satisfaction as a direct impact metric; Developer Experience Index (DXI) as indirect metric.

cat_activity.note: Percentage of AI-assisted PRs, share of AI-generated committed code, PRs merged per week.

cat_delivery.note: Thin basis: 'perceived rate of delivery' (Core 4 indirect metric); DORA only named as complement; PR cycle time only as an example (Claude).

cat_devex.note: DXI is listed, but no explicit use of the DevEx framework dimensions.

cat_survey.note: Perceptual metrics: developer satisfaction, perceived rate of delivery, change confidence.

evidence.quote: An AI measurement framework is a structured system for tracking, interpreting, and acting on the right signals when evaluating AI-assisted engineering.

Direct metrics offer immediate signals to evaluate the effectiveness of specific tools: AI-driven time savings (developer hours/week) Developer satisfaction Human-equivalent hours (HEH) of work completed by agents
evidence.loc: text source (Impact: how is AI affecting engineering productivity?)

evidence.quote: Indirect metrics, through regression and longitudinal analysis of DX Core 4 measures, surface longer-term benefits and hidden risks: PR throughput Perceived rate of delivery Developer Experience Index (DXI) Code maintainability Change confidence Change fail percentage
evidence.loc: text source (Impact: how is AI affecting engineering productivity?)

evidence.quote: Others are seeing serious degradation, with change failure rates swinging by as much as 2 percentage points, meaning some companies are shipping 50% more defects than before.
evidence.loc: text source (Why "we'll know it when we see it" doesn't work for AI ROI)

evidence.quote: Key utilization metrics include: AI tool usage (DAUs/WAUs) Percentage of PRs that are AI-assisted Percentage of committed code that is AI-generated Tasks assigned to agents
evidence.loc: text source (Utilization: how much are developers adopting and using AI tools?)

evidence.quote: PR throughput gap: daily AI users merge a median of 2.4 PRs per week, compared to 1.5 for non-users
evidence.loc: text source (Setting goals based on real industry data)
